name: Partying
overview: Scripture warns believers against seeking pleasure through partying and mirth as a primary pursuit, recognizing such enjoyment as ultimately vain (Ecclesiastes 2:1). Instead, Christians are called to live transformed lives, not conforming to worldly patterns of excess, such as rioting and drunkenness, but walking honestly and decently (Romans 12:2; Romans 13:13). The pursuit of approval should be directed toward God rather than men, avoiding behaviors that manifest the works of the flesh, including uncleanness and lasciviousness (Galatians 1:10; Galatians 5:19). Even in joyful occasions, like the wedding at Cana, Jesus’ involvement reminds us to honor God in all things, including celebrations (John 2:7).
